rows.caption_text:
Athletes are expected to be strong all the time, but being strong doesn’t mean you have to be okay every day. Behind the jersey, the wins, the highlights, and the smiles, we are still people. We deal with pressure, stress, expectations, and things that others may never know about.

During Suicide Prevention Month, I want athletes to know that it’s okay to go through hard times. It’s okay to have bad days. It’s okay to talk about how you feel and ask for help when you need it.

You are more than your sport. Your value is not based on how many points you score, how well you play, or how many games you win. At the end of the day, you are a person before you are an athlete, and you matter. 💚

#SuicidePreventionMonth #AthleteMentalHealth #MoreThanAnAthlete #YouMatter

rows.caption_text:
🤔Can you GUARANTEE that ball-handling drills will improve a player’s in-game ball control⁉️

💯For the first five years of my player-development career, I couldn’t. I was basically guessing. I had 3-ball drills, 2-ball drills, 1-ball drills, combination drills—you name it. We did more reps, added more difficulty, and players looked great doing them.

And I STILL had kids getting ripped at half court.

💎That’s when something clicked for me: ball control needed RULES. Just like shooting, movement, or anything else we expect to produce repeatable results, there had to be principles that governed WHY a player maintained control of the basketball—or lost it.

So instead of continuing to collect more drills, I started identifying those principles. I studied hand placement, foot movement and placement, hip movement and positioning, and ball movement and placement. The question became: If we can teach athletes to consistently adhere to these principles, can we consistently improve their ability to control the basketball when it actually matters?

That changed EVERYTHING for me.

It gave me the confidence to stop hoping a drill would transfer and start teaching players why they were able to control the ball in the first place. And I can honestly say that developing these principles is among the most important work I’ve done in player development.

Because drills give you something to DO. Principles teach you HOW, WHAT, WHEN, WHERE, and WHY to do it.

Tianna’s entire week was dedicated to applying these principles to the areas that can create the biggest growth in her ball control. We’ve seen some major jumps with her in the past, but based on what I saw this week, this one may exceed all of them.

Don’t just teach players more drills.

Teach them the principles that make the drills TRANSFER.

#Baylor #WBB #Basketball #WomensBasketball #WNBA

Shooting is the GREAT equalizer in basketball. But within shooting the dribble pull up is great equalizer.

Timing is key:

💎Never sacrifice quickness for distance. What that means is extended steps- to cover more ground- actually slows the dribble pull up. Get to the spot quickly and initiate the flinch response in your defender.

💎Match the pickup with the trail foot trigger- a dribble pull-ups don't gather early time to gather to match the trail foot (second foot to touch the ground)

rows.caption_text:
i first picked up a basketball in the 3rd grade. at the time it was just a ball in my hands and a game that i loved to play. i had no idea that the moment i picked up that ball would turn into a journey that would take me places some people can only dream of. i didn’t know the game would bless me with opportunities, experiences, and relationships that would shape my entire life.

there were so many days along the way where it felt impossible to imagine that i would be standing where i am today. the early mornings, the long practices, the sacrifices, the ups and the downs, and the moments where i questioned if i was really good enough. but through every challenge, every doubt, and every obstacle, i was never alone.

my mom, my gramma, and my little sister have been supporting me since the very beginning. my mom sacrificed so much of her own life just to make sure i could live out my dream. i’ll never forget the days she would leave work early just to make sure i was on time to practice. she gave up so much so that i could have opportunities she knew could change my life. because of her sacrifices, i was able to play at one of the most prestigious high schools in Missouri and be a part of something so special at Incarnate Word Academy. being apart of that was truly a blessing and something that helped shape me into the person and player i am today.

i worked so hard to put myself in positions to have opportunities in life, and that journey eventually led me to the university of kentucky. my freshman year was one of the toughest seasons of my life. mentally i was completely down and there were moments where i felt lost. but i refused to let that define me. i worked harder than ever because i knew i didn’t want to be in that same position again. my sophomore year i regained my confidence and it finally felt like i had found my old self again. 

but life isn't always how you paint it to be. my junior year brought a coaching change, and with that came learning a completely new system and, in many ways, learning myself all over again. there were moments where i struggled and didn't believe in myself the way i should have. (more will be in comments)

rows.caption_text:
It's simple👇

💎We can handle anything: luggage, weights, trash, etc. We can get it from place to place. But did we control it? Were we able to run with the luggage without it affecting our ability to move and maneuver quickly, efficiently, and seamlessly?

💎Control, by definition, is the ability to exercise authoritative and dominating influence over  something. For it to do what you want it to do when you want it to do it WITHOUT it resisting your efforts. 

✔️Seamless change of direction
✔️Agility with the ball
✔️Top end speed that is nearly equal with or without the ball
✔️Ability to keep the ball away from defenders without it affecting readiness to attack
✔️Confidence to stay in one place without having to dance

Tianna's understanding of ball control has grown significantly.

Now think about whether you or your athletes really possess ball control or are you just HANDLING the rock🤷🏽‍♂️💯

rows.caption_text:
🎓 OFFICIALLY A COLLEGE GRADUATE !!!

 
Three years, countless memories, and so much growth later, I’m walking away from SMU with a full heart and so much to be proud of. Graduating in just 3 years has taken a lot of hard work, sacrifice, and support from the incredible people around me.

To President Turner and Rick Hart (@ricklhart ), thank you for always supporting me personally and making me feel seen and valued, not just as a student-athlete but as a person. You both went above and beyond to create an environment where people like me could succeed, and I’ll always be thankful for your leadership and kindness throughout my time here.

To my amazing coaches, @coachtoyellewilson , @dparker4124 , @edwards__danielle , @coachaajr , and all the support staff (you know who you are): thank you for everything. You challenged me, believed in me, and invested in me far beyond basketball. You helped me grow through every high and low, and I always knew you had my back. Whether it was on the court, or just in life, your guidance shaped me into someone I’m proud to be. Thank you for your trust, your tough love, your encouragement, and your endless commitment to making me better. I’ll forever carry the lessons, values, and confidence you helped instill in me.

To the athletic trainers, strength staff, academic advisors, professors, and everyone behind the scenes — thank you for all the time, effort, and care you poured into me day in and day out. Whether it was helping me recover, stay strong, stay eligible, or stay focused, your impact was constant and appreciated more than words can express. You helped make the impossible feel possible, and I’m so thankful to have had you all in my corner.

SMU gave me more than just a degree, it gave me people and memories that changed my life. From day one, you all welcomed me with open arms, supported me through every moment, and turned what once felt unfamiliar into family. That’s something I’ll carry with me forever.

Now that I’ve Pony’d Up 🐎… let me go Sic ’Em 🐻

🎯4 "STATIONARY" Ball Control Stances that will take your handles through the ROOF‼️

Prepare for the demands of dynamic ball control by spicing up your stationary ball control #reals (not #drills)‼️

1. Players are increasing range of motion in hips, trunk, and shoulder, SPECIFICALLY for ball control. Players can absolutely prepare for the awkward and uncomfortable positions that players find themselves in. 

2. Players are working on proprioception in these positions while executing a skilled movement. 

3. We are DEEP FOCUSING because these positions force you to concentrate more deeply, i.e., in relaxing the arms to perform the dribble actions efficiently WHILE attempting to maintain balance. Controlling the breath helps stabilize the body while multi-tasking.

rows.caption_text: Lord only knows the sacrifices that were made to get to this point and the obstacles that were overcome that no one even knows about.  From playing pickup at the park with my dad  to selling lemonade to fundraise, it’s been a journey. I want to start off by thanking God for this talent he has given me and this opportunity to compete at a high level. I want to give a HUGE shoutout to my family for sacrificing EVERYTHING for me to get here. I want to thank my mom for always being there when I need her. I’m thankful for my dad for teaching me the game, the countless hours in the driveway, hours breaking down film and spending time with me after practice to get extra shots up. You finished what you started with me and I hope I’ve made you proud. Thank you to my little sister Melissa, the bleacher baby, for always supporting me and having my back in the stands. I want to thank all my teammates, past and present, for pushing me, and helping me grow as a player and a person. Thank you Coach Jr for taking a chance on me, and believing in me when I didn’t believe in myself. Thank you Coach Mike for pushing the best out of me the way only you know how.. and for feeding me too! Thank you Coach Patrick for helping me develop my shot and fundamental skills that have helped me get to this point. Thank you Coach Green for kicking my butt in workouts and always finding time to train when I call. Lastly, thank you to Coach Melissa who came out of retirement to pour into me and saw my potential at a young age. For that, I’ll forever be grateful. With that being said, I’m blessed to announce that I’ll be continuing my academic and athletic career at Bethune-Cookman University. #HAILWILDCATS❤️💛

rows.caption_text: On July 27th I tore my acl, meniscus, fractured a bone and subluxed my knee cap. I experienced one of the worst pains in my life. I was extremely devastated. Knowing I wouldn’t be touching the floor &  feeling like all the hard work I put in went down the drain in seconds. On August 7th I had surgery. I had so much support from my family, teammates, and the staff. I grew closer to my AT, and strengthened my bonds between my coaches and teammates. However I couldn’t walk for 6 weeks. During this time I noticed all the muscle in my leg was gone. I grew insecure, felt disassociated, depressed and so on but no matter what I worked hard. Basketball was my outlet and it was taken away from me but I acknowledged that it wasn’t the most important thing that has been taken from me in my life. I had to come to terms with that, my journey is beyond my understanding and God will show me why he made it that way sooner or later. Because of who I lost, I remain strong and highly motivated to come back greater in all aspects. With that being said I’ve been spending this time getting closer with God, growing, learning, molding into the woman I aspire to be, observing everything, and working on my mental. The last 6 months have been a ride. I hit milestones and accomplishments one day, and came across disappointment and frustration other days. There have been a  lot of ups and downs, but that’s life. Today, I had my first workout as I’m working back into the sport. Me 6 months ago felt like the time would never come, but here I am🖤.

Zamareya Jones (Wellcome Middle/Greenville, NC) 2024 4’10 PG – Zamareya Jones is a phenom that is super talented with a hesi-dribble, quick first step, and crossover that has made her an internet sensation. But as crazy it may seem, none of those are her best attribute. That would be her IQ, which is years beyond her current level. Using hand gestures and being extremely vocal on both sides of the ball, Zamareya has a natural leadership that players tend to follow without hesitation. We also couldn’t help but notice how competitive she was, never backing down from an opponent or giving up on a play. You won’t have to remember the name, because if you see her once you won’t ever forget her. 
#Hot100Girls #GetMeRecruited
